text: AgroViet 2026 opens in Hanoi with focus on green agriculture
The 26th International Agriculture Trade Fair (AgroViet 2026) officially opened in Hanoi on November 12 under the theme "Building on Tradition - Creating a Green Future".
The event brings together more than 100 domestic and international organisations and businesses, with 250 standard exhibition booths.
The international section features 100 booths from companies in China, South Korea, Japan, Australia, the United States and several ASEAN countries.
The domestic exhibition area represents 26 provinces and cities, including Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Can Tho, Lai Chau, Phu Tho, Thanh Hoa, Tuyen Quang and Bac Ninh.

Exhibits include key national and local agricultural products, export-oriented goods, products with competitive advantages, products certified under the One Commune One Product (OCOP) program, and high-tech agricultural products.
Visitors can also explore crop, livestock and aquaculture varieties, biofertilisers, biological pesticides, agricultural machinery, greenhouse equipment and drip-irrigation systems.

Post-harvest technologies and services are another major focus, including preliminary processing, food processing and preservation equipment, packaging, logistics, cold storage, product traceability labels, distribution networks and e-commerce platforms.
Around 50 booths showcase agricultural machinery, food-processing equipment, organic fertilisers, quality seeds, pesticides and products for veterinary, livestock and aquaculture industries.

Companies from Japan, China and Vietnam are also presenting aquaponics models combining vegetable cultivation and fish farming, alongside automated irrigation systems, greenhouse materials, agricultural films and packaging solutions.

A new feature of this year's fair is its expanded focus on environmental protection technologies and equipment, with dedicated exhibition space for science and technology products and innovative start-ups.

Domestic booths are organised by product groups linked to value chains, while digital platforms are being used to promote exhibitors and collect and classify visitor data to facilitate more targeted business connections.
The exhibition also highlights achievements in the agriculture and environment sectors, alongside solutions for digital and green transformation.
